brief: Three bases arranged around an empty spot, with a bay tray standing in that spot.

requirements.requirement: Three bases arranged around an empty spot
requirements.evidence: Hex base pieces at (0,0,0) (pre-existing), (-1,1,0) and (-2,1,0). Each touches the empty cell (-1,0,0), which is left empty for the tray.

requirements.requirement: A bay tray standing in that empty spot
requirements.evidence: Bay bay:0#-1,0#bay4 (Full bay tray, solid, south bay variant hex-bin-bay-s-full-solid) sits in the empty cell (-1,0,0), bolted to the three bases. check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built three full hex bases at (0,0), (-1,1) and (-2,1) on level 0, around the empty cell (-1,0). A solid full bay tray sits in that cell. I also capped the open faces and locked the joints per house rules. check_build is clean with meshClash clear. No props or soil were added, since the brief did not ask for them.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
